t:
(a) Sense of Congress.—It is the sense of Congress that the Department has not implemented all of the recommendations made by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) and the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) related to embassy security and 
that some recommendations may yield potentially significant cost savings to the Department. 
    (b) Briefing.—The Secretary shall provide a briefing to the appropriate congressional committees detailing the rationale for not implementing recommendations made by the GAO and OIG related to embassy security or those that may yield significant cost savings to the Department, if implemented.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a required briefing and reference to GAO/OIG recommendations amounts to consultation before a decision. But every actor here (the Secretary, congressional committees, GAO, and OIG) is inside the federal government, and the definition excludes reports or briefings to Congress. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: The Secretary shall provide a briefing to the appropriate congressional committees detailing the rationale for not implementing recommendations made by the GAO and OIG related to embassy security

opus.w: The only interactions are recommendations from GAO and the OIG (both federal bodies) and a briefing to congressional committees (inside the federal government). No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, or right to sue. It may look like oversight-based participation, but that interaction never leaves the federal government, so it fails the definition's single test of whether an outside party is involved.
opus.s: The Secretary shall provide a briefing to the appropriate congressional committees detailing the rationale for not implementing recommendations made by the GAO and OIG related to embassy security
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this section looks procedural: GAO and OIG recommendations shape a federal decision, and the Secretary must brief congressional committees on why those recommendations weren't adopted. But every actor here is inside the federal government. GAO is a legislative-branch agency, the OIG is part of the Department, and the congressional committees are Congress. No outside party is involved, so this is not participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary to brief congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation. The recommendations come from the GAO and OIG, which are also internal federal agencies, not outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall provide a briefing to the appropriate congressional committees detailing the rationale for not implementing recommendations made by the GAO and OIG related to embassy security or those that may yield significant cost savings to the Department, if implemented.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary must provide a briefing to Congress, this constitutes "participation" or consultation. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is INSIDE the federal government, and reports or briefings to Congress are not considered participation. The GAO and OIG are also internal federal entities, so their recommendations do not constitute outside participation.
